findings.title: The one-line-per-seed report format that this round's prose asserts is itself asserted by no test
findings.failure_scenario: The delta's whole point is the sentence at :268-272 and the archive row claiming 'Every FAILING SEED is reported on one line -- its first violation plus a count of the rest, not one line per violation'. That format is built at :197-206 and constrained by nothing: `failing` is only ever asserted `isEmpty()`, so on a green run its contents are never read, and on a red run JUnit prints whatever was built. A later edit reverts the sweep to one line per violation, the 353 KB / 2000-line XML blowup the comment at :190-196 records comes back, the seed gets buried again, and the whole suite stays green. This is the same class of defect this task's own baseline entry names -- a claim in prose with no assertion under it -- now attached to the sentence written to fix a claim in prose.
findings.surviving_mutation: Delete the ternary at :203-205 (the `" (+" + (run.violations().size() - 1) + " more on this seed)"` suffix), or replace the whole `failing.add(...)` block with `for (var v : run.violations()) failing.add("seed " + seed + ": " + v.invariant());`. MEASURED: `theInvariantsHoldAcrossEverySeed` passes on a clean tree either way, because `failing` is empty and no test ever inspects a non-empty one. `aBrokenReaderViewREACHESTheSweepsVerdict` asserts on `run.violations()`, not on `failing`, so it does not cover the format either.
findings.recommendation: DO NOT FIX IN THIS ROUND. Rounds 9-11 of this task have been prose-fixing minors; adding a fixture that drives one seed to two violations and asserts the emitted line is a behaviour change to the test in a round whose delta is prose. A backlog row, or fold it into M4.50 which already replaces the trace the report reads.

findings.title: The failing gate in the review packet is M0.91, reproduced by the review instruction itself -- not a defect in this commit
findings.failure_scenario: `review.sh context` exited 1 on `check-harness-tests.sh` before emitting the diff, reporting `294 tests completed, 1 failed`. MEASURED in the review tree: `REVIEW_ROUND_BUDGET=20 ./gradlew -p buildSrc test --rerun-tasks` gives `ReviewRoundBudgetTest > thePacketREFUSESToOpenAnotherRoundPastTheBudget(Path) FAILED`; the same command without the variable is BUILD SUCCESSFUL, 294 tests, 0 failed. The variable is exported to the gate loop by the very command the reviewer was told to run, so every over-budget round of this task will see a red gate that has nothing to do with the staged bytes -- and a reviewer who does not chase it either skips the round or files it against this commit. M0.91's corrected note is right on the mechanism: `ReviewRoundBudgetTest.java:150` calls `packet(dir, rc, "REVIEW_ROUND_BUDGET", "99")`, so the `remove()` cannot go in `packet()` at :73-84.
findings.surviving_mutation: n/a -- this is a verification of a claim the delta changed, not a weak assertion. The claim in the M0.91 row as edited this round is accurate and I could not falsify it.
findings.recommendation: Nothing to change here. Recorded so the red gate on the packet is not read as a defect in the staged bytes.

notes:
Delta since the round-10 tree (924876a) is prose only: baselines/review.txt, backlog.md, backlog-done.md, backlog-notes.md, and javadoc/comment/.as() text in CommitProtocolSweepTest.java. No assertion changed value, direction or subject -- `failing` is still `isEmpty()`, the six SEEDS*k floors, the SEEDS==1000 guard, the readersChecked and ackEvents floors and `ackFloorAlwaysZero` are byte-identical. Nothing was weakened.

Round-10 minor 1 is genuinely fixed and the fix is true: the report at :197-206 builds exactly one entry per failing seed, first violation plus a count, and the new .as() at :268-272 states that the rest are NOT listed. The previous string was false as I reported it.

Round-10 minor 2: I stand by not taking it. An abort on the last line is a behaviour change to the test, and M0.89's grep over tracked files is the stronger rung-1 remedy for the same hole. It does not belong in this commit.

VERIFIED BY MEASUREMENT in my own tree, not by reading:
- The sweep runs green: `sweep: 1000 seeds in 15724 ms, 74172 readers judged, budget 60000 ms`. The 74,172 in the archive row is exact. 15.7s sits just outside the javadoc's stated 14.6/15.1/15.4s spread; I am NOT raising that, because the comment records named runs and explicitly argues the spread is why the figure is reported and not asserted -- adding a fifth number is the failure mode this task's baseline entry describes.
- The row's new clause 'SEEDS ITSELF IS ASSERTED WHENEVER -Dsweep.seeds IS UNSET' holds: rewriting :89 to `Integer.getInteger("sweep.seeds", 10)` with the property unset gives `CommitProtocolSweepTest > theInvariantsHoldAcrossEverySeed() FAILED`. The guard kills the mutation it was written for.
- The row's other new clause -- M0.89 owns the tracked-file route -- is consistent: the guard keys on `System.getProperty("sweep.seeds") == null`, and `providers.systemProperty("sweep.seeds")` at binjava.java-conventions.gradle.kts:130-131 resolves `systemProp.sweep.seeds` from gradle.properties, so a tracked file does skip the guard and no assertion in the test can see it.
- The M0.90 dead-band figures are now internally consistent: 300s @Timeout / ~15s is 'near 20x' in the backlog row, 60s BUDGET_MILLIS / ~15s is 'near 4x' in the in-test comment.

Open findings from earlier rounds: all of the majors listed in the packet were raised against hashes 0f062ae, 28bc2c0, 322f180, 88f502e, a5f2698 and aae3b85 and are closed in the staged bytes -- the addAll is pinned through the loop by `aBrokenReaderViewREACHESTheSweepsVerdict`, the slot-0 CONTINUE is emitted and pinned by `ackFloorAlwaysZero` plus the ackEvents floor, `-Dsweep.seeds` is forwarded, the floors are SEEDS*k, and the SEEDS guard sits on the resolved value not on DEFAULT_SEEDS. None of them re-opened in this delta.
